topics.label: Scalar and Vector Potential
topics.summary: If curl F = 0 a scalar potential φ exists with F = ∇φ; if div F = 0 a vector potential A exists with F = curl A. Shows how to find φ by successive integration and matching.

topics.label: Line Integrals
topics.summary: The line integral of F along a curve C parametrized by r(t) gives the work done by F; derived from a Riemann sum of F·Δr and computed with a single-variable integral over t.

topics.label: Green’s Theorem in the Plane
topics.summary: Relates the counterclockwise circulation around a closed plane curve to a double integral of ∂N/∂x − ∂M/∂y, justified by internal edges cancelling in a grid of tiny rectangles.

topics.label: Surfaces and Surface Integrals
topics.summary: The flux integral of F·n over a surface S measures how much F flows through it; explains why the normal is needed and why dS differs from dA for a tilted surface.

topics.label: Stokes’ Theorem
topics.summary: Circulation of F around a closed curve C equals the flux of curl F through any surface bounded by C; Green’s Theorem lifted to 3-D, so the simplest surface can be chosen.

topics.label: Volume Integrals; The Gauss Divergence Theorem
topics.summary: Volume integrals are ordinary triple integrals; the Divergence Theorem equates outward flux through a closed surface with the volume integral of div F, with a cube-verification example.

subtopics.label: Volume Integrals
subtopics.summary: Scalar and vector volume integrals are mechanically the triple integrals of Module 2, used as the right side of the Divergence Theorem.

subtopics.label: The Gauss Divergence Theorem
subtopics.summary: Closed-surface flux equals the integral of div F over the enclosed solid, shown by cancelling shared faces of tiny cubes; verified on the unit cube.

topics.label: Module 3 — Master Summary
topics.summary: Tables summarising the gradient, divergence and curl operators (input, output, zero-condition) and what Green’s, Stokes’ and Gauss Divergence theorems convert and require.
